Feast-day recipes

Roasted Nuts and Dried Fruits

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 8-10Prep 10 minCook 15 min

Roasted nuts and dried fruits are a traditional treat served during Yalda Night, an ancient Persian festival celebrating the winter solstice. This mix symbolizes the warmth and light of the sun during the longest night of the year and is enjoyed by families as they gather to share stories and poetry.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups raw almonds (300 g)
  • 1 cup raw walnuts (120 g)
  • 1 cup raw pistachios, shelled (120 g)
  • 1 cup dried apricots, chopped (130 g)
  • 1 cup dried figs, chopped (130 g)
  • 1/2 cup dried cranberries (60 g)
  • 2 tablespoons honey (30 ml)
  • 1 tablespoon unsalted butter (14 g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. Spread the almonds, walnuts, and pistachios evenly on a baking sheet.
  3. Roast the nuts in the oven for 10-12 minutes, stirring halfway through to prevent burning.
  4. While the nuts roast, melt the butter and honey together in a small saucepan over low heat.
  5. Remove the nuts from the oven and transfer them to a mixing bowl.
  6. Pour the honey-butter mixture over the warm nuts and toss to coat evenly.
  7. Add the ground cinnamon and salt, mixing well to distribute the spices.
  8. Allow the nuts to cool slightly, then add the chopped dried apricots, figs, and dried cranberries.
  9. Mix gently to combine all ingredients.
  10. Serve the roasted nuts and dried fruits warm or at room temperature as a festive snack for Yalda Night.

Tips

  • For a spicier mix, add a pinch of ground cardamom or nutmeg.
  • Use raw, unsalted nuts for the best control over flavor and saltiness.
  • Store leftovers in an airtight container at room temperature for up to one week.
